data.body:
SWEEP ADDENDUM — a seventh gap ticket, and the epic-close policy decision.

7. seraphic-taming-terrier (3ed6-b264-e1ae-41a0) discovered_from this epic, relates_to frangible-irongray-adouri — rebar's LLM gate operations (close with the completion gate, review-plan, verify-completion) emit NO output between start and verdict, so a supervisor treating silence as no-progress kills a healthy run. This is the root cause of the S3 executor agent's death: it was killed by a 600s stall watchdog at the epic-close step with all nine of its changes already landed, stranding the epic and one story in_progress with every descendant closed. Independently reproduced twice in the completing session: the S3 close blew a 600s foreground timeout and emitted only unrelated enrich_drain warnings before its final line, and review-plan on this epic did the same.

The two tooling bugs COMPOUND, which is why they are cross-linked: seraphic-taming-terrier makes a SUCCESSFUL close look hung, while frangible-irongray-adouri makes a CRASHED close look successful (ImportError, then exit 0). A supervisor that survives the silence may then be told exit 0 by a close that never happened. Anyone automating rebar closes should read them together.

EPIC-CLOSE POLICY, decided by the operator: the epic closes now with all seven gaps FILED, LINKED and dispositioned rather than fixed. Rationale recorded for the next reader: the gaps are discovered_from links, not children, so rebar's structural open-children guard does not block this close — the requirement was a judgment call, not a tool constraint. Three of the seven are already in_progress. One, insectile-modest-martin, is deliberately NOT closeable: it exists to constrain the reconcile.py extraction RP-03 S5 has not yet performed, so closing it would destroy its only purpose. The three RP-02-discovered defects (alert dedup, the stale idempotency patch target, and remote Jira writes during preview/dry-run create recovery) are LATENT and PRE-EXISTING — this epic surfaced them by characterising documented behaviour, it did not introduce them, and fixing them inside a pure-extraction epic was explicitly out of scope.

CLOSE MECHANICS worth recording, since both gates fired legitimately on this close: the first attempt was refused with 'plan-review close gate: stale-pin-drift — reviewed related-ticket material is stale ... targets: 486a-69ef-6370-48ff child stale-pin-drift, fc1c-1b08-70c2-4afb child stale-pin-drift'. That was CORRECT: this epic's attestation pins its children's material, and both S2 and S3 had their plans legitimately corrected during execution (S2's phantom double-bind safety-abort; S3's run_differs.py-to-reconcile.py ordering error). Remediated by re-running review-plan on the epic, which returned certified — not by --force. The close also had to run from a git worktree at 0b851c8103 using the checkout's venv build, because the shared main checkout must never be fast-forwarded to satisfy a close and the global packaged build is broken per gap 6.
